canonical_question: Why does the 1400 °C sample show an 'almost linear increase' and 'general corrosion' instead of passivation, suggesting a failure of the protective mechanism?

question_variants.question: Why does the 1400 °C sample show an 'almost linear increase' and 'general corrosion' instead of passivation, suggesting a failure of the protective mechanism?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text explicitly states that the carburized layer of the 1400 °C sample exhibited an 'almost linear increase of the current density under the increase of the potential', which the reader interprets as 'general corrosion'. The text notes that 'alloy components gradually dissolved' in this sample, confirming the lack of a clear passivation plateau and suggesting a failure of the protective mechanism.

answers.answer: The 1400 °C sample shows an 'almost linear increase of the current density under the increase of the potential', and the text explicitly states that 'alloy components gradually dissolved' in this sample, indicating general corrosion and the absence of a passivation plateau.
answers.measurement_outcome: almost linear increase of the current density, alloy components gradually dissolved
answers.mechanism: general corrosion due to lack of passivation
evidence_spans: Their volume fraction decreases when the SPS temperature increases and accounts for 21.5 vol.% at 1300 °C and 11.5 vol.% at 1400 °C.
The coarse inclusions can serve as sources of crack initiation in the BCC-matrix.
